issues.feedback: The spec deletes `ralph/daemon/<task_id>` before `git worktree prune`. If `git worktree remove` falls back to direct directory deletion, Git still considers the branch checked out and `git branch -D` fails. Delete should happen after prune (or retry after prune).

`remove_worktree()` currently returns early when the worktree path does not exist. With the proposed approach, stale branches in this state would not be deleted. To meet "no manual git branch -D", branch deletion should be attempted even if the directory is already gone.

Using `git branch --list` for machine parsing is brittle (human-formatted output with markers/spaces). Prefer plumbing commands: `git show-ref --verify refs/heads/<branch>` for existence and `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) refs/heads/ralph/daemon` for sweeping.
The doc labels cleanup as recommended/optional, but acceptance criteria 5 and 6 make it mandatory. Scope should be explicitly one or the other.

The proposed retry test seeds a `pending` task, but the real restart path is `in_progress -> pending` reconciliation plus redispatch. Add an end-to-end restart test that starts from `in_progress` with a stale branch and validates successful redispatch.

Asserting the per-task worktree directory exists after `--single-iteration` is unstable because runtime cleanup removes worktrees on terminal state. Assert dispatch success/state transition (and branch behavior) instead.
